target_customer: Regulated financial companies in lending, debt collection, money transmission, mortgage and insurance that need state licenses
problem: Getting and keeping state licenses means manual filings, renewals and regulator follow ups run through spreadsheets, email and expensive outside firms.
business_model: B2B SaaS and services with annual contracts; company says it has signed six figure annual contracts (self-reported)

founders.name: Aaron Chen
prior_employers: a16z-backed DeFi startup (unnamed on YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page: product engineer, won ETHGlobal New York and Delhi. Team is from UC Berkeley per YC page; no individual degree given.

founders.name: He Song
previous_startups: Company scaled to a $15M valuation as a freshman; later launched a token at a $60M valuation (YC page, outcomes not stated)
founders.background_notes: Built a crypto lending product at Berkeley; met co-founder in Blockchain at Berkeley.

competitors.what: Regulation-as-data platform for US state money transmitter requirements

competitors.name: FS Vector APPROVED
competitors.what: Licensing and examination platform with NMLS sync for application tracking and renewals

competitors.name: Brico
competitors.what: AI licensing platform for payments and crypto companies, partner of Modern Treasury

technical_complexity.rationale: Requires encoding multi-state licensing rules, regulator portal workflows and agents that file reliably. Hard parts are accuracy and regulatory knowledge rather than novel research.

defensibility.rationale: Licenses and filing history live in the system once adopted, and regulatory knowledge accumulates. Several incumbents and startups already sell similar tooling.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent move against Payna found in the sources reviewed.

market_need_then: Company reports live debt collection and lending customers and six figure annual contracts. The Model Money Transmission Modernization Act is reshaping state exams per FS Vector, adding compliance work.

identity.voice_and_tone: tagline: From the first license to the hundredth

branding.brand_signature: Tagline From the first license to the hundredth

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand found. The name resembles payment words and the legal entity on the site footer reads Paena Technologies, Inc., a small inconsistency.

outcome_analysis: Payna is an active Winter 2026 company with no exit. The founders say they hit manual licensing pain first hand while building a crypto lending product, which gives founder-market fit, and they report early paying customers. No verified funding or later outcome exists, and competitors such as FS Vector and Brico already sell licensing automation.
notes: Unverified funding: aggregators list $500K seed (Jan 2026) and a separate $125K seed entry on Dealroom, which conflict; no primary source, so no round recorded. Sources disagree on founding year (2025 vs 2026); YC page says 2025. Outcome search found nothing about shutdown or acquisition. Brico and FS Vector pages are undated. Competitors dated near founding are thin.
